ic_name: ARM Serial Wire Debug (SWD) — ADIv5 (ARM IHI 0031C)
notes: ADIv5 SWD is a digital wire-level debug-access protocol; no analog reference / trim / calibration is part of the architecture. Practical board-bring-up characterizations focus on: SWCLK frequency margin (does the SoC's SW-DP still ACK correctly at the chosen SWCLK frequency?), SWDIO signal integrity (especially when the debug probe has a long cable or the target has a level-translator), Turnaround timing (CTRL/STAT.TRNCNT increase may be needed for slow drivers), SWDIO direction-change glitches (push-pull vs open-drain target drivers behave differently), and SWO trace pin baud-rate calibration (separate from SWD but commonly tuned at bring-up). None of these are protocol-mandated calibration steps — they are board / probe-design verifications.
board_bring_up_characterizations_typical: SWCLK frequency sweep — start at 1 MHz and increase until the target stops ACKing OK reliably; back off to ~50% of the max for production headroom.
Signal integrity on SWDIO — verify rise/fall times at the target's SWDIO pin meet the SoC's tSU/tH; especially important on long flex-cable connections (TC2050 needle probes).

Turnaround cycle calibration — for slow-driver SoCs or stacked level-translators, increase CTRL/STAT.TRNCNT from 0 (1 cycle) to 1-3 (2-4 cycles) to give the SoC longer to release SWDIO before the host drives.
Pull-up sizing on SWDIO — verify the pull-up keeps SWDIO HIGH (idle) when the debug probe is disconnected; typical 4.7 kΩ to 10 kΩ.
Pull-down sizing on SWCLK — verify quiescent state; typical 10 kΩ if present (some boards leave SWCLK floating).
VDD-IO level matching — verify the probe's SWDIO/SWCLK voltage matches the target VDD-IO; auto-sensing probes (J-Link, ST-Link V3) handle this automatically.
SWO trace pin baud-rate calibration — for ITM trace, the SWO baud rate is set by the TPIU's ASYNCCLKDIV register; host probe must match this baud (typical 1-50 Mbps).
Line-reset margin — verify ≥ 50-cycle line reset works at all SWCLK frequencies in the working range; some buggy SoCs accept 50 cycles only at low frequencies.
Mode-switch reliability — for SWJ-DP, verify JTAG-to-SWD and SWD-to-JTAG selection sequences succeed reliably across temperature + voltage corner.
Multi-drop bus loading — for ADIv5.2 multi-drop SWD, verify all targets' SWDIO pads can co-exist without contention; check total bus capacitance + termination.
